result.topic_en: Developable surfaces: from the condition pr − q² = 0, Gauss derives that the first derivatives t, u of z are functions of v = tx + uy − z (Lagrange's form), and then rewrites the line element ds² in terms of p, q, r.
result.transcription:
Abwicklungsfähige Flächen.
$\frac{dz}{dx} = t \quad \frac{dz}{dy} = u$
$\frac{ddz}{dx^2} = p, \ \frac{ddz}{dxdy} = q, \ \frac{ddz}{dy^2} = r$
Bedingungsgleichung
$pr - qq = 0$
Man setze
$tx + uy - z = v$
Man hat
$dt = p\,dx + [-q\,dy-] q\,dy$ [?]
$du = q\,dx + r\,dy$
$dv = (px+qy)\,dx + (qx+ry)\,dy$
Hieraus
$q\,dt = p\,du$
$r\,dt = q\,du$
$p\,dv = (px+qy)\,dt$
$q\,dv = (qx+ry)\,dt = (px+qy)\,du$
$r\,dv = (qx+ry)\,du$
$dv = x\,dt + y\,du$

Es sind demnach t und u Functionen von v
und dabei $z = tx + uy - v$
$1 = \frac{dt}{dv}\cdot x + \frac{du}{dv}\cdot y$
Dies ist die Form welche Lagrange gegeben hat:
Ist nun ferner ein Linienelement ds
$ds = \sqrt{(1+tt)dx^2 + 2tu\,dx\,dy + (1+uu)\,dy^2}$
Also
$ds^2 = \frac{p\,dx^2 + 2q\,dx\,dy + r\,dy^2}{(1+uu)p - 2tuq + (1+tt)r}(1+tt+uu) + \frac{p[tu\,dx + (1+uu)\,dy]^2 - 2q[(tu\,dx + (1+uu)\,dy)\cdot((1+tt)\,dx + tu\,dy)] + r((1+tt)\,dx + tu\,dy)^2}{(1+uu)p - 2tuq + (1+tt)r}$

methods.what: Condition for a developable surface: the Hessian determinant of z vanishes
Legendre-type substitution v = tx + uy − z and its differential
Using pr = q² to derive proportionality relations between dt, du, dv
Differential identity giving t, u as functions of v
Lagrange's form of a developable surface: z = tx + uy − v with t, u functions of v
Line element of the surface z(x,y) in terms of the first derivatives
Decomposition of ds² using the second fundamental form p dx² + 2q dx dy + r dy²

items.quote: Es sind demnach t und u Functionen von v
items.english: Accordingly t and u are functions of v
